tagline: how a runtime remembers what it has already computed
source: Mechanism and figures as published in the paper. Nothing on this page was measured here.

panels.title: What has already been computed, kept as a tree
panels.sub: the KV cache is indexed by a radix tree over token sequences, so a shared prefix is computed once and stays computed
panels.note: an arriving request walks the tree as far as it matches, and only pays for the rest
panels.scale: an illustrative program, not a measurement

labels: every request pays for its own prefix
chart.axis: tokens computed, in the illustration beside

panels.title: The order requests run in is a cache decision
panels.sub: the scheduler runs the request that shares the longest prefix with what is already in the tree
panels.note: cache-aware scheduling turns a prefix that would be recomputed per request into one that is computed once
panels.tail: same requests, same answers, a different order

chart.axis: times the prefix is computed, for the queue beside

panels.title: When the grammar already knows the next tokens
panels.sub: constrained decoding against a compressed finite state machine: a span the schema forces can be filled in one step
panels.note: the model is only asked for the tokens the constraint has not already decided
panels.bottom: compressed FSM: the forced spans are jumped
panels.tail: and the paper's headline: up to 6.4x on structured programs

chart.axis: decode steps for the span beside

panels.title: What the tree came to
panels.sub: a program that calls a model many times stops paying for the part of the prompt it keeps repeating
panels.note: the gain is largest exactly where programs are structured: agents, chains of thought, JSON, batched few-shot
bullets: RadixAttention: the shared prefix is computed once and kept in the tree
cache-aware scheduling: the queue is ordered so that it can be reused
compressed FSM: the tokens a grammar has already decided are not decoded

chart.axis: throughput on structured language model programs, relative to the systems the paper compares against
